title: NASA appoints Christina Koch as acting deputy chief engineer
excerpt: The astronaut will transition to a management role on November 1, 2026, following the retirement of Katherine Van Hooser.
bodyHtml:
NASA announced on October 13, 2026, that astronaut Christina Koch will serve as the agency's acting deputy chief engineer. Koch will begin the new role on Sunday, November 1, 2026.

The appointment follows the retirement of Katherine Van Hooser, who will conclude more than 35 years of service to the agency on Wednesday, October 21, 2026. In her new position, Koch will help lead the engineering community and support technical oversight, mission readiness, and engineering excellence across the agency’s programs and projects.

With this transition to management astronaut status, Koch will no longer be eligible for future spaceflight assignments. Koch previously served as a mission specialist on the Artemis II mission in April 2026. Before her selection as an astronaut in 2013, her experience included scientific field engineering in Antarctica and the Arctic. She began her NASA career as an electrical engineer at the agency’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, developing scientific instruments for space missions.
